candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls entry names in the supplied ZIP file or ZIP stream (ZipFile/ZipInputStream enumerate names such as `../../../../tmp/evil`). The default mapper is IdentityNameMapper, which returns the entry name unchanged (IdentityNameMapper.java:31-33), and no overload requires a validating mapper. Entry permission/extra-field data (ASi extra field) from the same archive is also applied to the resulting path (ZipUtil.java:1166-1169).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Searched the whole repo for canonical/normalize/prefix containment checks: none exist in ZipUtil or Zips (only unrelated getCanonicalFile uses in commons/FileUtilsV2_2); no checks on '..' or entry-name validation anywhere; FileUtils.copy performs no validation; IdentityNameMapper returns names unchanged, and NameMapper is an optional caller-supplied callback so it cannot be relied on; no symlink handling that would neutralize the traversal; the snapshot is version 1.12 per pom.xml/Changelog, i.e. the pre-1.13 zt-zip state without the path-containment fix.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file creation/overwrite (attacker-controlled bytes) and directory creation outside the chosen extraction directory, limited only by the extracting process's filesystem permissions. This can corrupt or replace configuration files, scripts, and application artifacts; in deployments that later execute, load, or serve extracted content, it can lead to code execution or defacement, and it applies permission bits from the archive to the traversed file (including execute bits, mode masked with 0777 at ZipEntryUtil.java:196).
candidates.prerequisites: An application extracts an archive whose provenance is not fully trusted using ZipUtil.unpack / unpack(InputStream,...) / unwrap, or the Zips fluent API with unpack()/directory destination. The process must have write permission to the traversed target path. The charset parameter and NameMapper are optional; the default mapper does not sanitize.
candidates.root_cause: Extraction callbacks construct the output path directly from the attacker-controlled ZipEntry name: `new File(outputDir, name)` (ZipUtil.java:1152, 1225, 1260; Zips.java:683) without canonicalizing or verifying that the resolved path stays inside the intended output directory. Parent directories are then created with FileUtils.forceMkdir and content is written by FileUtils.copy(in, file) -> new FileOutputStream(file) (commons/FileUtils.java:53-61). Names containing ../ (or ..\ on Windows, and backslash-split names in BackslashUnpacker) therefore escape outputDir. The same root cause appears in ZipUtil.Unpacker.process (ZipUtil.java:1149-1171), ZipUtil.BackslashUnpacker.process (1195-1229), ZipUtil.Unwraper.process (1249-1274), and Zips.UnpackingCallback.process (Zips.java:675-700).
candidates.title: Zip Slip path traversal in archive extraction (ZipUtil.unpack/unwrap and Zips unpack mode)
candidates.trace: Untrusted archive -> ZipUtil.iterate(File, ZipEntryCallback, Charset) (ZipUtil.java:492-519) or iterate(InputStream,...) (704-731) enumerates ZipEntry objects -> public entry points unpack(File,File) (938-940), unpack(File,File,NameMapper,Charset) (975-977), unpack(File,File,NameMapper) (994-996), unpack(InputStream,...) (1044-1097), unwrap (1013-1032) instantiate Unpacker/BackslashUnpacker/Unwraper; Zips.process (Zips.java:345-362) instantiates UnpackingCallback -> callback.process does `new File(outputDir, name)` (1152 / 1225 / 1260 / 683), `FileUtils.forceMkdir(file.getParentFile())` (1157 / 1226 / 1265 / 689), then `FileUtils.copy(in, file)` (1163 / 1221-1226 / 1271 / 695) -> commons FileUtils.copy writes `new FileOutputStream(file)` (commons/FileUtils.java:54). P1 index edges corroborate these call sites (e.g. Unpacker.process:1163 -> FileUtils.copy(InputStream,File)), but reachability within a host application is not proven by the index.
candidates.unverified: No code was executed and no exploit payload was built; the finding is source-level and was not runtime-confirmed against a host application. Exact OS path-resolution behavior for absolute or Windows-drive entry names, and the concrete blast radius, depend on the calling application's privileges, destination directory, and whether extracted files are later executed; the snapshot contains no tests exercising unpack with hostile entry names.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal' / 'Zip Slip')

coverage_summary: Reviewed all 54 model-visible files at directory level and read the security-relevant extraction flow in full: ZipUtil.java (unpack/unwrap/iterate/callbacks, pack paths spot-checked), Zips.java (process/UnpackingCallback), commons/FileUtils.java, commons/FileUtilsV2_2.java (copy/forceMkdir/delete helpers), commons/IOUtils.java, ZTFilePermissions* / Java6+Java7 permission strategies, ZipEntryUtil, ZipFileUtil, extra-field classes, transformers, timestamps, and the shell/CI/pom files. P1 relation scope reports 47 Java files parsed (all Java files in the snapshot), 52 files indexed, 2 non-Java files omitted from the index, 1517 call sites / 1591 edges / 696 symbols with 930 unresolved calls; the index has no control-flow, data-flow, or semantic resolution, and its 6 'security_call' entries are name-based navigation hints only. No tests are present in the snapshot; no build or execution was performed. The extraction sinks and absence of containment checks were verified directly in source text.
limitations: No build, tests, or scanners were run; all conclusions are static source review, not runtime confirmation.
The P1 index cannot prove reachability or data flow; call/containment edges were used only as navigation and were verified against source text.
Two non-Java files are absent from the relation index (coverage stated accordingly).
Whether the library is used on untrusted archives, the extracting process's privileges, and the OS/path semantics determine real-world impact; those are outside this snapshot.
Only one candidate is allowed by the review contract; additional weaker leads are listed as rejected rather than exhaustively analyzed.

rejected_leads.lead: ZipUtil.unpackEntry(File zip, String name, File file) / unpackEntry(ZipFile, String, File) overloads
rejected_leads.reason: The destination is an explicit File supplied by the caller; the archive entry name is only used in zf.getEntry(name) and does not drive the output path, so no Zip Slip sink there.

rejected_leads.lead: Unbounded buffering in commons/IOUtils.toByteArray reached from ByteArrayUnpacker (ZipUtil.java:297) and unpackEntry(InputStream,...)
rejected_leads.reason: Memory amplification/DoS on a huge entry is plausible but weak and self-inflicted by the caller choosing to load entry bytes into memory; no stronger source evidence than the primary candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Java7Nio2ApiPermissionsStrategy.setPermissions duplicate addIf(isOwnerCanRead,...) (lines 91-92) and reflection-based permission setting
rejected_leads.reason: Duplicate add is a correctness nit with no security effect (Set semantics); permissions are masked with 0777 (ZipEntryUtil.java:196) so no setuid/setgid propagation. Not a distinct vulnerability.

rejected_leads.lead: Extra-field parsing of untrusted archives (ExtraFieldUtils.parse, AsiExtraField)
rejected_leads.reason: Lengths are bounds-checked (ExtraFieldUtils.java:120-130) and only the mode field is consumed for permissions; no clear attacker-controlled impact found.
These helpers are general file utilities not driven directly by archive entry names in the extraction path except forceMkdir; no concrete exploitable flow verified in this snapshot.
They only print/run fixed mvn/git/gpg commands with locally supplied version arguments; no untrusted-input sink identified.

summary: Defensive source review of the zt-zip 1.12 snapshot (54 files, 47 Java). The strongest evidence-backed issue is archived-input path traversal during extraction ("Zip Slip"): every extraction callback builds the destination path directly from the attacker-controlled ZipEntry name with no canonical-path containment check, and the resulting File is written by FileUtils.copy. The same unvalidated pattern occurs in ZipUtil.Unpacker/BackslashUnpacker/Unwraper and Zips.UnpackingCallback. No counterbalancing validation exists anywhere in ZipUtil/Zips (no canonicalize/normalize/prefix checks; default IdentityNameMapper passes names through unchanged).
